blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Removing the public `status` field breaks partner integrations with no deprecation) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (The breaking rename is not marked BREAKING nor tells users what to do) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-3 (No rollout order keeping old and new consumers working side by side) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`OrderResponse.status` becomes `OrderResponse.state`; the old name is not
kept. The OpenAPI file is regenerated.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The field is renamed in place
findings.recommendation: Apply expand and contract — return both `status` and `state` for a deprecation period, mark `status` deprecated in openapi.yaml, and remove it only in a later change once partners have moved; record the dated removal plan in the design.
findings.title: Removing the public `status` field breaks partner integrations with no deprecation

findings.evidence: - Changed: The order's `status` field is now called `state`.
findings.recommendation: Mark the item **BREAKING** in the release note and in What Changes, and say what consumers must do (read `state` instead of `status`, by which date the old field disappears).
findings.title: The breaking rename is not marked BREAKING nor tells users what to do

findings.evidence: - [ ] 1.1 Rename the field and regenerate `openapi.yaml`, verified by tests "A paid order" and "An unknown order"
findings.recommendation: Split the work into ordered tasks — add `state` alongside `status` and deprecate `status` (with a test that both fields are returned), announce to partners, then a separate later task or change that removes `status`.
findings.title: No rollout order keeping old and new consumers working side by side

findings.recommendation: Plan a major version bump (2.0.0) of the OpenAPI `info.version` and `package.json` when `status` is removed, or keep the release minor by only adding `state` and deprecating `status`.
findings.title: The API version is not bumped for a breaking change
